title: Does Physical Restraint Use Prevent Falls in Nursing Homes?
text: Physical restraint use nursing homes common controversial practice. One frequently cited justifications fall prevention. analysis examines whether facility-level restraint prevalence associated lower fall rates, using longitudinal data 2016 2025 across nursing homes province Trento, Italy.

title: Does Physical Restraint Use Prevent Falls in Nursing Homes?
text: association restraint falls strongly heterogeneous across facility–sector pairs. 47 pairs, 15 show credible benefit (restrained residents fall less), 8 show credible harm, rest uncertain — effect changes sign across facilities. new, unobserved facility–sector pair, posterior predictive probability benefit 61%. major-outcome falls (clinically important ones), average effect compatible zero predictive evidence benefit weak (P ≈ 0.60). falls minor outcomes, pairs show credible harm (10) credible benefit (6).

title: Physical Restraint Use and Falls in Nursing Homes
text: Data come Indicare Salute Lab, quality monitoring system managed UPIPA (Unione Provinciale Istituzioni Per l’Assistenza). Observations facility × care-sector × month combinations, pairing restraint indicator (2.1, point prevalence) three nested fall indicators: total falls (1.1), falls outcome (1.3), falls major outcome fractures (1.5). main research question whether physical restraint use associated reduction falls — whether association clinically meaningful.

title: Physical Restraint Use and Falls in Nursing Homes
text: restraint–fall association strongly heterogeneous across facility–sector pairs generalizable: 47 facility–sector pairs, ~15 show credible benefit, ~8 credible harm, ~24 uncertain — effect changes sign across facilities. new, unobserved facility, posterior predictive probability benefit ~61%. meaningful evidence restraint reduces major-outcome falls (clinically important ones): average effect compatible zero. minor-outcome falls, pairs show credible harm (10) credible benefit (6). Effectiveness restraint fall-prevention strategy evaluated case case, based characteristics facility, confirmed individual-level data.

Restraint prevalence follows per-pair quadratic time trend (orthogonalized, standardized); fall rates partially pooled across facility–sector pairs via Beta hyperpriors, outcome shares via non-centered logistic-normal hierarchy. Model development proceeded 12 iterations Bayes factors (bridge sampling) posterior predictive checks; full workflow documented data-raw/model-development.qmd.
